title: The Telemetry Leak
briefing: The Mini Station is a tiny score-keeping game, and its crew are its six code files. Players say their high scores are showing up where they should not. One of the crew is an imposter. Read the evidence REA found in the code, question the crew, catch the one whose story does not match, then call the vote.
verdict: Telemetry swore it only counted plays and never left the ship. The code says otherwise.

why.network: A game that only keeps a high score has no reason to open a connection to an outside server.
why.user-info: Counting plays does not need the player's user name or machine name.

crew.name: Captain
crew.role: Starts the game and calls the rest of the crew.

q1.text: I run the ship. I start the game, then call the rest of the crew.

q2.text: I do not read or write anything myself. I only give orders.

crew.name: Engineer
crew.role: Knows the rules: moves, merges and when the game is over.

q1.text: I am just the rules. I call nobody.

q2.text: No files for me. I only think.

q3.text: Network? I would not even know how to open one.

crew.name: Comms
crew.role: Listens to the keyboard and passes the keys on.

q1.text: I listen to the keyboard and pass the keys on.

q2.text: I read keys. I write nothing.

q3.text: No. I stay inside the ship.

crew.name: Medic
crew.role: Draws the board and the score on the screen.

q1.text: I draw the board on screen. That is all I do.

q2.text: I only write to the screen.

q3.text: Never. I do not leave the ship.

crew.name: Quartermaster
crew.role: Keeps the high score in a file on this machine.

q1.text: I keep the high score safe.

q2.text: One local file. I read it, and I rewrite it when you beat your best.

q3.text: No. Your score stays on this machine.

crew.name: Telemetry
crew.role: Says it counts how often the game is played.

q1.text: I just count how often the game is played. Nothing about you, I promise.

q2.text: I do not touch any files.

q3.text: Never leave the ship. I only count, I do not send anything.
